judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence consideration/insuring recital; the only oddity ('THES POLICY') is an OCR artifact rather than a drafting defect, and 'subject to all the terms' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a lead-in that expressly subordinates itself to the rest of the policy, so it harmonises with the coverage forms and endorsements rather than competing with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely descriptive statement that the policy consists of the coverage parts for which a premium is shown; 'may be subject to adjustment' is vague but does no operative work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Premium Audit condition (Section IV.5 CGL) and the Calculation of Premium endorsement, which supply the adjustment mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Insurance at the described premises applies only for the coverages shown below' is a short exclusive limitation, but the term 'described premises' is defined by the schedule and is not itself ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the blanket building/contents/business income limits in the same Declarations covering nine separate locations, which raises a modest question whether coverage is per-premises or blanket.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short schedule note; 'subject to the General Aggregate Limit' is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Declarations that show a separate $2,000,000 Products-Completed Operations Aggregate and against Definition 16.b.(3), which excludes from the products hazard any operation whose classification says products-completed operations are subject to the General Aggregate — a genuine cross-reference tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple, definite grant of a cancellation right to the first Named Insured; 'advance written notice' is unquantified but the insured's own right is not a likely battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel cover-jacket version (c072) and with the Kansas Changes endorsement IL 02 61, which amends only paragraph 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear two-tier notice periods (10/30 days) with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 2 of this condition is expressly replaced by IL 02 61 (Kansas Changes — Cancellation and Nonrenewal), which adds a statement-of-reasons requirement and limits permissible grounds, so the unamended text now contradicts the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Last mailing address known to us' is definite and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the duplicate at c074 and the nonrenewal notice provision in IL 02 61 B.2; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two flat declaratory sentences fixing the effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Installment Payments condition, which contemplates a cancellation notice specifying the date, and with the Kansas endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The refund may be less than pro rata' leaves the short-rate calculation unstated, a mild indeterminacy, but the rest is mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision fixes the refund basis, so nothing contradicts it; the Premiums condition simply names the payee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single evidentiary rule; 'sufficient proof of notice' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim at c077 and in IL 02 61 B.2 without variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration plus no-oral-modification clause; 'contains all the agreements' is boilerplate and definite, though it sits oddly with 'the first Named Insured is authorized to make changes'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is in fact amended by numerous endorsements, all issued by the insurer, which is exactly what the clause requires, so it coheres with the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR garbling aside, the audit right is definite as to scope and time (policy period plus three years).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the CGL Premium Audit condition and the record-keeping duties in the Duties In The Event Of Loss conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text says 'We have the right to' but then disclaims obligation, and it cross-refers to 'Paragraphs 1. and 2.' while the provision is lettered a., b., c. — a numbering mismatch that makes the carve-outs hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel cover-jacket printing at c080 reads 'We have the right but are not obligated to' and omits the boiler/elevator certification carve-out, so the two printings of the same condition do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short numbered duties; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c081 and the CGL Premium Audit condition, which also directs return premium to the first Named Insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An anti-assignment clause with a death exception; 'proper temporary custody' is slightly loose but the operative rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the CGL Section II.2.c–d, which makes the legal representative and temporary custodian insureds on the same terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming provision, and 'subject to the laws of your state' leaves reinstatement discretionary — loose but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duplicate at c083 says the notice will specify only 'the date' while this one says 'the date and time', and the Kansas endorsement requires a statement of reasons that this condition does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A truncated applicability lead-in; as reproduced it is a fragment, but its function is purely introductory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fuller cover-jacket version at c084 adds that the Coverage Part is also subject to the Common Policy Conditions and the coverage-form Loss Conditions, so the two lead-ins differ in scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void in any case of fraud' and 'intentionally conceal or misrepresent a material fact' are strong but standard; materiality is a question of fact rather than construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (Kansas Changes — Concealment, Misrepresentation or Fraud) expressly replaces this condition with a narrower 'we will not pay' formulation, so the unamended text directly contradicts the controlling endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences, both definite; 'beyond your direction or control' is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 supersedes the Control Of Property Condition, but only where coverage is provided for townhouse buildings, leaving a small question whether the substitution reaches these apartment buildings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single anti-stacking sentence with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the Other Insurance condition and with the several Additional Coverages that are expressly 'additional insurance', which are carve-outs rather than contradictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all of the terms' is broad, but the two-year limitation is a definite number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A (Kansas Changes) replaces this very condition and substitutes five years, so as printed the policy states two irreconcilable suit-limitation periods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any revision that would broaden the coverage' is somewhat open-ended, but the 45-day window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses mid-term broadening, so nothing in the instrument pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence badly mangled by OCR, but its rule — bailees take no benefit — is unambiguous in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with the Personal Property Of Others coverage, which pays for the owner's account rather than the bailee's.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pro-rata and excess rules turning on whether other insurance is 'subject to the same plan, terms, conditions and provisions' — a phrase that can be argued about in a real dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Property Not Covered k. (property more specifically described elsewhere) and with the excess wording in the Non-Owned Detached Trailers extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise temporal and geographic limitation with an enumerated territory list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The CGL definition of 'coverage territory' is broader, but that definition governs a different coverage part, so no genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Must do nothing after loss to impair them' plus an enumerated post-loss waiver list is definite; the enumerated list against no catch-all is a mild expressio unius point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second printing at c094 says 'to or from whom we make payment' rather than 'to or for whom', and CP 01 01 E substitutes a different waiver rule for the Builders' Risk form, so the instrument carries variant texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, heavily defined exclusion; every operative term is separately defined in the companion paragraph, which cuts against ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that it modifies the CGL, Liquor Liability and Auto parts, none of which is the property coverage at issue, and it duplicates the Nuclear Hazard exclusion in CP 10 30 without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions are so badly truncated in this printing ('Hazardous properties include radioacti\ explosive propertles') that several defined terms are incomplete as reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined terms are used only inside the same endorsement, so any incoherence is internal to it rather than across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, mechanical premium-computation rule; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated at c092 and consistent with the CGL Premium Audit condition; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proportionate part of any policyholder's dividend if declared' is conditional but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These are 'Conditions Applicable to State Automobile Mutual Insurance Company', yet the Declarations name State Auto Property and Casualty Insurance Company as the issuing company, leaving it unclear whether the mutual-company conditions apply at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise statement of membership and meeting rights, with time and place fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same mismatch as the other mutual-company conditions: the named insurer on the Declarations is the stock property and casualty company, not the mutual whose members are described here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence non-assessability warranty; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says no premium other than that stated is payable, which sits awkwardly with the CGL Premium Audit condition making the advance premium a deposit subject to audit adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading instruction and pronoun key; definitional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the identical preamble in CP 00 30 and with the definitions sections it points to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core insuring clause turns on 'direct physical loss of or damage to' and 'at the premises described in the Declarations', phrases capable of argument but here used in their settled sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly qualified by Property Not Covered, the Causes of Loss form, Limits of Insurance and the Coinsurance condition, so it is designed to be read with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Building, meaning the building or structure described in the Declarations' plus long enumerated inclusions; the enumerations are detailed and the catch-alls ('all other personal property owned by you and used in your business') are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations describe the premises only as 'BLANKET APARTMENTS' across nine locations, so the reference to 'the building described in the Declarations' is not squarely matched by the schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A seventeen-item exclusion list containing broad residual phrases such as 'other evidences of debt' and 'other paved surfaces', which invites ejusdem generis argument about the reach of each catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item k. (property more specifically described elsewhere) interacts with the Other Insurance condition, and item n. is expressly qualified by the Electronic Data Additional Coverage, both of which are drafted as coordinated carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to the applicable Causes of Loss form; nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations do identify CP 10 30 Special Form, so the cross-reference resolves cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but arithmetically specified, with worked examples that fix the meaning of the 25% cap and the additional $10,000.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Debris removal overlaps the Ordinance Or Law exclusion's reference to 'the cost of removing its debris', which could be argued to cut across this Additional Coverage after a total fire loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two precise conditions (while being moved; within 30 days) with no open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with Limits Of Insurance, which says preservation payments do not increase the limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed $1,000 sublimit with two enumerated triggers; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly reconciled with Limits Of Insurance, which states this sublimit is in addition to the Limits of Insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on the defined term 'pollutants', which is famously broad, but the coverage grant, the 180-day notice and the $10,000 cap are all precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with the Debris Removal carve-out for pollutant extraction and with Limits Of Insurance, which makes this sublimit additional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap in e.(6) is internally complex — '$10,000 or 5% of the Limit of Insurance ... whichever is less' with a wholly different blanket-limit formula ('5% times the value of the damaged building ... times the applicable coinsurance percentage') — and e.(8) concedes that the Ordinance or Law Exclusion may 'conflict' with it, which is an express admission of contestable reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against the Ordinance Or Law exclusion (c101), the Loss Payment condition b. and the Replacement Cost provision f. (c067), all of which say the cost to repair does not include code-upgrade costs; reconciling those with this grant is precisely the kind of whole-instrument problem a court has to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed, with a defined meaning for electronic data borrowed from Property Not Covered and a fixed $2,500 annual cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly keyed to whichever Causes of Loss form applies, and consistent with Property Not Covered n., which carves out this Additional Coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional trigger ('a Coinsurance percentage of 80% or more or a Value Reporting period symbol') that is precise, plus a 100-foot proximity rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show 100% coinsurance, so the trigger is satisfied; the closing statement that Coinsurance does not apply to the Extensions is repeated at c051.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed sublimits and a three-event termination rule; 'intended for similar use' is mildly open but the structure is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Business Income Newly Acquired Locations extension, which uses a 50% coinsurance trigger rather than 80%, but the two apply to different coverage forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, with a fixed $2,500 sublimit and an express theft carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Covered Property c. (personal property of others) and its owner-account payment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise about duplicates, the $2,500 cap and which costs are additional insurance versus subject to the BPP limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly coordinated with Property Not Covered o. and with the Electronic Data definition; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Temporarily at a location you do not own, lease or operate' is a soft boundary, but the exclusions and $10,000 cap are firm.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the 100-foot rule in the Extensions lead-in and with the Property In Transit extension in CP 10 30 F.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated five-peril list with fixed caps; the enumeration is closed, which limits argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 D expressly revises this very Extension to replace '$250' with '$500' per tree, shrub or plant, so the printed figure here is superseded and the two texts state different numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative conditions, two express carve-outs and a fixed $5,000 cap; entirely determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its excess-insurance sentence dovetails with the Other Insurance condition and with Property Not Covered p.(2)(d).
